title: metadata-protocol: duplicatePackage leaves a copied permission set's `fields` keys (OBJECT.FIELD) naming the SOURCE object, so the duplicate's field-level security applies to the source
body:
Filing gate ①, finding class (b): a declared producer contract the producer breaks, measured on a real kernel. Filed by `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · `huangyiirene` · session `session_01YRp5z4kK6vgYkrdH97ztsy`, from #23511's dev report (PR #23525, out-of-scope finding 1). ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and lane are triage's.

`Seam: spec:PermissionSetSchema.fields (a record keyed OBJECT.FIELD) → runtime:ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.duplicatePackage (deepRewrite) | consumer: the copy's field-level security`

`reach:` `protocol.duplicatePackage` on a real kernel (ObjectKernel + ObjectQLPlugin, memory driver) at PR #23525's head `e9c2bc9ad`. This is the method the packages duplicate route calls. The HTTP door was not driven.

**Reader who acts:** triage, to grade and route. The fix lands in `duplicatePackage` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) once PR #23525 lands. That PR makes the `objects` map's keys follow the renamed objects; this card covers the composite `fields` keys.

## What happens (measured)

The source permission set is `dupsrc_fls`, with:
- `objects: { dupsrc_customer: … }`;
- `fields: { 'dupsrc_customer.full_name': { readable: true, editable: false } }`.

It is copied as `dupdst_fls`. In the copy, `objects` is keyed `dupdst_customer` (after PR #23525), but `fields` is still keyed `'dupsrc_customer.full_name'`. So the copy's field-level rules name the SOURCE object, and the duplicate's object gets none of them. Before PR #23525, neither map's keys followed the rename.

## The contract

`duplicatePackage`'s docblock (ADR-0070 D4) promises "rewriting every intra-package reference". The composite `OBJECT.FIELD` key form is not one that the derived object-reference site index models. PR #23525's record-key rewrite covers only keys that are bare object names, at object-reference properties.

## What done looks like

- In a copied permission set's `fields`, a key's object part follows the renamed object (`dupsrc_customer.full_name` → `dupdst_customer.full_name`). This covers both a prefixed object and a bare one renamed by #23511.
- A field part that merely shares the object's name stays unchanged.
- Pin it on a real kernel, with a negative control: a key naming an object outside the package keeps its name.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included: `duplicatePackage permission set fields key object.field not rewritten copy field-level security names source object` → 7 hits:
- #23292, #22455, #21861, #21794, #21789, #20027 (all closed) concern permission-set write-through, locks, gates, and the managed-object blanket;
- #3661 (closed) concerns the `/meta` FLS mask.

None of them is the duplicate's `fields` key rewrite.

Dedupe words: duplicatePackage permission fields key object.field not rewritten; duplicate field-level security names source object; duplicatePackage composite key re-namespacing.
